title: Open TIA whitelist Entry as writable in .NET Framework
goal: Fix TiaV21Worker whitelist self-sync so RegistryKey is opened as writable while requesting only SetValue and QueryValues on the existing Registry64 Entry key.
scope: Coding-agent scope is exactly src/TiaV21Worker/WhitelistManager.cs and no other file.

In WhitelistManager.SynchronizeWhitelist, replace the RegistryKey.OpenSubKey overload that supplies only RegistryRights with the overload that explicitly uses RegistryKeyPermissionCheck.ReadWriteSubTree together with the same RegistryRights.SetValue | RegistryRights.QueryValues.

Preserve RegistryHive.LocalMachine, RegistryView.Registry64, the existing Entry key path, whitelist value names, hash/date semantics, bootstrap-required fail-closed behavior, and all TIA connection ordering.

Do not broaden registry rights beyond SetValue | QueryValues and do not change bootstrap ACLs, parent Siemens keys, workflow files, runner configuration, secrets, generator/domain/compiler code, or IndustrialMDE.

requirements: The Entry key is opened with RegistryKeyPermissionCheck.ReadWriteSubTree and rights exactly RegistryRights.SetValue | RegistryRights.QueryValues.
Whitelist writes remain limited to Path, DateModified, and FileHash beneath TiaV21Worker.exe\Entry.
Bootstrap-required remains the fail-closed result for actual access denial or missing key.
No candidate Windows/TIA execution occurs; candidate validation is Linux-only.
Primary connected ChatGPT performs independent exact-SHA CODE_REVIEW because the candidate is authored by the coding agent.
tia: After merge, run trusted-main /run-olq-001 from issue #19 without changing the registry ACL.
No interactive Openness access (0033:000666) dialog may appear.
